mechanism: One codec row is shared by DEFINE-MESSAGE and the wallet's DEFINE-WDB-KEY/DEFINE-WDB-VALUE: :var-string reads with (map 'string #'code-char (br-read-var-bytes br)) and writes with (bb-write-var-bytes bb (map '(vector (unsigned-byte 8)) #'char-code value)) (src/serialization/message-macro.lisp:114-116). That is Latin-1, not bytes. A character above U+00FF has a CHAR-CODE that does not fit the (unsigned-byte 8) result vector, so the WRITE is a raw TYPE-ERROR; a byte sequence that is really UTF-8 comes back as one character per byte. Core's std::basic_string serializer is a compact-size length followed by the raw bytes with no character decoding at all (refs/bitcoin/src/serialize.h:787-793 at d3056bc), and walletdb's address-book 'name' records hold the label's bytes verbatim. The RPC layer decodes the request body as UTF-8 (src/rpc/server.lisp), so a label with any non-Latin-1 character reaches wallet-set-address-book as a string with code points above 255.
consequence: setlabel (and getnewaddress with a label) fails outright for every non-Latin-1 label -- all CJK, Cyrillic, emoji -- and fails badly: the TYPE-ERROR escapes the wallet store, handle-single-request catches it as a generic error and returns -32603 'Internal error: The value 20013 is not of type (UNSIGNED-BYTE 8)...' (src/rpc/server.lisp:407-420), which reads as a node bug rather than an unsupported label. Worse than the error, the write is PARTIALLY APPLIED: wallet-set-address-book sets the in-memory addr-book-entry-label before the leveldb-put that throws (src/wallet/wallet.lisp:672-687), so until the next restart the wallet reports a label that is not in the wallet file. A Latin-1 label does survive our own round trip, but it is stored as ONE byte where Core writes the two UTF-8 bytes, so the record diverges from Core's walletdb encoding for every accented character. Bounded: labels only; descriptors and addresses are ASCII, and the outbound user agent is already sanitized -- so S3, not a wrong consensus or index answer.
evidence: Container /Users/sen/common-lisp/bl-ga11v-misc-s3b, warm image. (a) Codec, direct: (bitcoin-lisp.wallet::wdb-string-value "hi") -> #(2 104 105); with (code-char 233) -> #(1 233) (Core would write the two UTF-8 bytes C3 A9); with (code-char 20013) -> TYPE-ERROR 'The value 20013 is not of type (UNSIGNED-BYTE 8) when setting an element of (ARRAY (UNSIGNED-BYTE 8))'. Reading Core-shaped UTF-8 back: (wdb-parse-string-value #(2 195 169)) -> a two-character string with char codes (195 169) instead of one U+00E9. (b) End to end through the real dispatcher (probe build/ga11probe/label.lisp, with-wallet-chain-node + a regtest wallet): (bl.rpc:dispatch-rpc-method node "setlabel" (list addr <two CJK chars>)) -> (:ERROR TYPE-ERROR ...); the same call with (code-char 233) -> (:OK NIL). (c) Partial apply (probe build/ga11probe/label3.lisp): after the failed wallet-set-address-book, (:ERR (:ERROR TYPE-ERROR) :INMEM-LABEL-CODES (20013) :ON-DISK :ABSENT) -- the in-memory address book holds the label the wallet file does not. Ours: src/serialization/message-macro.lisp:114-116; src/wallet/wallet-store.lisp:96, :340; src/wallet/wallet.lisp:672-687. Core: serialize.h:787-793.
fix_shape: Make the wire/DB string codec byte-exact the way Core's is, and keep the character conversion at the edge. Split the single :var-string row into a byte-level primitive plus an explicit UTF-8 codec: write (babel/sb-ext:string-to-octets value :external-format :utf-8) and read (octets-to-string bytes :external-format :utf-8 with a replacement policy for invalid sequences), so a label round-trips as the bytes Core would have written and a peer-supplied user agent full of arbitrary bytes cannot signal. Both DEFINE-MESSAGE and DEFINE-WDB-VALUE take the change from the one shared row, which is also why the fix must be verified on both surfaces. Because the decode direction is fed by untrusted peer bytes, the reader must never signal on an invalid UTF-8 sequence -- decode with replacement, not strictly. Finally, make wallet-set-address-book persist BEFORE it mutates the in-memory book (or wrap the pair) so a failed write cannot leave the two disagreeing. A regression test should assert one label per class -- ASCII, Latin-1, CJK, emoji -- comes back from the store byte-identical to Core's UTF-8 encoding.
